Key features arguing against a 1p/19q co-deleted oligodendroglioma include the presence of marked enhancement ('Enhancement Quality': 'Marked'), a large volume of necrosis ('NCR Volume (mL)': 9.638), and a thick enhancing margin ('Thickness of enhancing margin': '>3mm'). Oligodendrogliomas typically present with minimal to no enhancement and rarely show necrosis. The highly aggressive features seen in this case are characteristic of a high-grade astrocytoma or glioblastoma, making a 1p/19q co-deletion extremely unlikely.
